input.quote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, nothing in this Agreement grants or may grant MSL any rights or licenses in any preexisting intellectual property of IBM except that IBM grants MSL a royalty-free license to use the confidential information disclosed in connection with this Agreement under the AECI referenced in 13.2 necessary to manufacture Products solely for IBM.
input.rationale: Every licence grant in this agreement runs from us (IBM) to the counterparty (MSL), not the reverse: §13.3(a) gives MSL only a narrow royalty-free right to use IBM confidential information to manufacture Products solely for IBM; §24.1(a) and the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement §§5-6 likewise grant MSL limited, use-restricted rights in IBM software, Loaned Programs and Licensed Internal Code. Those restrictions benefit our side and are not flagged. Our own position is stronger than the preferred licence position rather than weaker: under §13.1 IBM "assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products", plus assignment of MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes, and MSL is barred from using proprietary processes for the Products absent written agreement — so we hold ownership rather than a revocable licence, and there is no grant to us that MSL can revoke at will or that excludes our affiliates or contractors. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording but are noted only: the agreement contains no IBM affiliate/"Related Company" extension (the concept is used only for MSL) and no express licence-back of MSL background IP for transition to a replacement manufacturer; successor/assignment mechanics sit in §16.2 and §16.5 (with MSL warranting that any acquirer assumes performance) and are addressed under the assignment rule rather than double-flagged here.
